title: Balancing Work, School, and Projects: A Simple Schedule

cover.alt: Conceptual folded ribbon alternating bursts of coding activity with calm gaps for rest.

figures.title: Two work rhythms, compared on the same dimensions
figures.summary: The article describes the author’s experience rather than prescribing one schedule for everyone.

items.label: Timing
items.detail: A steady routine uses recurring blocks; the sprint pattern varies with interest and available time.

items.label: Motivation
items.detail: The routine emphasizes habit; the sprint pattern emphasizes intrinsic interest.

items.label: Pauses
items.detail: The routine has planned breaks; the sprint pattern allows longer gaps between active periods.

items.label: Risk
items.detail: Rigid blocks can feel forced; interest-driven work can leave long gaps when momentum fades.

figures.caption: A qualitative comparison from the post, not a measured productivity ranking.

figures.title: A sprint still needs a finish line
figures.summary: When a project matters enough to ship, the article describes a concrete sequence.

items.label: Make room
items.detail: Use the available evening or weekend time.

items.label: Focus
items.detail: Close distractions and work on that slice.

items.label: Check the live result
items.detail: Deploy and test the real URL.

items.label: Pause
items.detail: Ship the change and step back.

figures.caption: The author’s stated shipping pattern. Rest is part of the cycle, not a failed work session.
